splits.splitA: train 2018-2023, eval 2024 (single held-out year; HEADLINE regime pools 2018-2024 with 2018-2023 from G1 gold bundle — eval-year-retrained signal diluted across 7 years)
splits.splitB: train 2018-2024, eval 2025 OOS (clean single held-out year; OOS regime = 2025 only — pure retrained signal)

pace_feature.feature_added: cross_channel_min_pace = NaN-safe min(qs_best_raw, lr_best_raw) appended to driver vector in _driver_vector; 24 features total

notes.headline_caveat: Headline score pools 2018-2024: 2018-2023 from G1 gold bundle (CONTROL and +PACE identical for those years); 2024 is the ONLY freshly retrained year in splitA. The +0.0232 headline lift is diluted across 7 years — the per-year 2024 lift is larger.
notes.oos_caveat: OOS 2025 is a PURE signal from splitB retrain: +PACE rw=0.7700 essentially equals the 0.7643 ceiling and beats the CONTROL rw=0.5868 by +0.1832. This is the strongest evidence.
notes.seed: Both CONTROL and +PACE retrains used --seed 0; differ ONLY in feature vector (23 vs 24 features)

verdict_rationale: On OOS 2025, +PACE rises from 0.5868 to 0.7700 — a +0.1832 lift that reaches the ceiling (0.7643). CONTROL reproduces the expected deficit. This pattern confirms hypothesis (a): the cross-channel min-pace ordering signal was ABSENT from the control feature vector and IS learnable once supplied as an input. The headline signal is diluted (only 1 of 7 years retrained) but still shows +0.0232 directional lift. Commander decides final verdict.
